body: I took a look into this recently and it appears to be a side effect of how this feature was implemented. I can't find any tests to confirm this was the intended behavior, so yes, I think it's a bug and should be fixed. Looks like it'll be some time during the RC period for Version 8.

I'm facing this exact same issue while dealing with deeplinking in a big enterprise app.
Example: native side of the app wants to open a particular page and on the web side, we have our own deeplinking routing redirects so that both sides are not forced to always point to the same urls (easier to maintain this way).

Due to this though, it is not possible to preserve/merge the query params unless we hack and intercept the request and then **manually** add the queryParams ourselves. If this becomes an added feature, it would be greatly appreciated as our codebase would become a lot cleaner! 😄 

@jasonaden, not wanting to put pressure or anything, just looking for info. Since Angular 8 is already out (I can't update yet because the app is written in Ionic 4 and Angular 8 is is not supported as of yet): has this been attended to?

The amount of issues that have been opened, and the comments discussing it, since 2016, is proof enough that this feature is badly needed by many, many people.

Is it difficult to implement such a feature?

issue.title: Can't redirect to url with query params while preserving initial query params

milestone.title: needsTriage

issue.body:
# Bug Report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package @angular/router ### Is this a regression? No ### Description When redirecting a path to a 2nd path which uses query params the initial query params are discarded. Example: ``` const routes: Routes = [{ path: 'used-cars', redirectTo: '/cars?used=true', }]; @NgModule({ imports: [RouterModule.forRoot(routes, { paramsInheritanceStrategy: 'always' })], exports: [RouterModule] }) export class AppRoutingModule { } ``` (Note that the leading slash is required as discussed in https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/9921) If I now navigate to `/used-cars` I will be redirected to `/cars?used=true` which is the expected behaviour. However, if I navigate to `/used-cars?color=yellow` I will be redirected to the same url which is not the expected behaviour. Instead, it should redirect to `/cars?used=true&color=yellow` since the `paramsInheritanceStrategy` in the `ExtraOptions` is set to `'always'`. ## Minimal Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-hsyujd?file=src/app/app.module.ts ## Exception or Error - ## Your Environment **Angular Version:**

issue.body:
… string or UrlTree

This commit updates the logic around `Route.redirectTo` to enable using a function to create the redirect. This function can return a string, ands acts the same as previous string redirects, or a `UrlTree`, which will act as an absolute redirect.

To be useful, the redirect function needs access to the params and data. Today, developers can access these in their redirect strings, for example `{path: ':id', redirectTo: '/user/:id'}`. Unfortunately, developers only have access to params and data on the _current route_ today in the redirect strings. The params and data in the `RedirectFn` give developers access to anything from the matched parent routes as well. This is done as the same way as param and data aggregation later on (https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/897f014785578d87bc655ea6ae9e113653960f50/packages/router/src/router_state.ts#L236-L278). In order to accomplish this, we inherit params and data while matching, after the `ActivatedRouteSnapshot` is created for the matched route rather than waiting until the end.

The `RedirectFunction` does not return the full
`ActivatedRouteSnapshot` interface. Some things are not accurately known at the route matching phase. For example, resolvers are not run until later, so any resolved title would not be populated. The same goes for lazy loaded components. The is also true for all the snapshots up to the root, so properties that include parents (root, parent, pathFromRoot) are also excluded. And naturally, the full route matching hasn't yet happened so firstChild and children are not available either.

fixes #13373
resolves #28661 (though not for the redirect string - you would return a `UrlTree` from the function)
